system_description.narrative_title: US–Iran Escalation and Strait of Hormuz Attacks
system_description.narrative_summary: A rapid cycle of US strikes on Iranian targets and reciprocal Iranian attacks — including assaults on commercial tankers and reported mine warfare in the Strait of Hormuz — is disrupting maritime traffic and pushing global oil prices higher. Treated as an open system, the episode exchanges kinetic actions, economic flows (oil, insurance, shipping), political signaling (US domestic politics, regional allies), and information flows (media, sanctions) with feedback loops that can amplify escalation or force de-escalation. The situation couples military operations, commercial logistics and energy markets, creating cross-domain vulnerabilities that can propagate through global supply chains and regional security architectures.
system_description.scope: Within the system boundary: US military strikes on Iran and Iranian retaliatory operations; attacks on commercial tankers, mine warfare and transit disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz; oil/commodity flows and price/insurance effects; US sanctions and diplomatic/isolation campaigns; regional state reactions (Saudi, UAE, Qatar, Gulf actors) and related maritime logistics (ship-to-ship transfers, rerouting).
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical and energy-security system (international politics, global oil markets, and maritime commerce).
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil markets and commodity trading
Maritime security, shipping insurance and logistics
Regional Middle East security architecture (Gulf states, proxies, bases)
US domestic politics and electoral-calculation drivers

variables.name: Kinetic engagement intensity
variables.description: Measures the aggregate intensity and frequency of armed strikes and direct military exchanges in the maritime and adjacent operational theatre.

variables.name: Maritime vessel transit rate
variables.description: Measures the number of commercial vessels transiting the chokepoint per unit time.

variables.name: Crude oil throughput rate
variables.description: Measures the volumetric flow of crude oil (barrels per day) moving through the maritime corridor.

variables.name: Global oil price level
variables.description: Measures the prevailing market price level for benchmark crude reflecting supply/demand and risk premia.

variables.name: Shipping insurance premium level
variables.description: Measures the average insurance premium charged for commercial shipping transits through the risky maritime zone.

variables.name: Vessel rerouting fraction
variables.description: Measures the proportion of scheduled transits diverted to alternative longer routes or ship-to-ship transfers per time period.

variables.name: Maritime mine incident rate
variables.description: Measures the frequency of mine-laying, mine encounters, and mine-related damage incidents in the corridor.

variables.name: Maritime security control balance
variables.description: Measures the relative degree of effective control or denial of freedom of navigation across the maritime chokepoint.

variables.name: Sanctions enforcement intensity
variables.description: Measures the rate and strictness of economic enforcement actions applied against targeted trade and financial flows.

variables.name: Diplomatic pressure level
variables.description: Measures the aggregate intensity of diplomatic actions aimed at isolating or constraining actors involved in the dispute.

variables.name: Regional security cohesion
variables.description: Measures the degree of coordination and alignment among proximate states on security and operational responses in the theatre.

variables.name: Market risk perception
variables.description: Measures aggregated market participants' perceived probability and severity of supply disruptions due to the security environment.

variables.name: Oil supply chain disruption level
variables.description: Measures the degree to which upstream and downstream commercial logistics and refinery feedstocks are disrupted by the maritime situation.

variables.name: Ship-to-ship transfer rate
variables.description: Measures the frequency and volume of cargo transfers conducted at sea as an alternative to port-to-port transits.

variables.name: Tanker capacity utilization
variables.description: Measures the proportion of available tanker carrying capacity in use or held in reserve relative to total fleet capacity.

variables.name: Information flow intensity
variables.description: Measures the rate and reach of media, official messaging, and information dissemination that amplify situational awareness and narratives.

catalysts.title: Sustained US strike campaign
catalysts.description: Continuation and expansion of US strikes on Iranian targets aiming to degrade capabilities and pressure Tehran.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple headlines: 'US launches further strikes on Iran', 'U.S. Tries to Squeeze Iran With New Strikes' (2026-09-01/02).

catalysts.title: Iranian reciprocal strikes
catalysts.description: Tehran conducts retaliatory strikes against US forces, allied assets, or shipping in response to US actions.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Iran's president says Tehran will reciprocate', 'Iran hits back' after US strikes (2026-09-01/02/03).

catalysts.title: Escalation in naval mine incidents
catalysts.description: Increased mine-laying, mine strikes, and disputed mine reports that restrict safe navigation in the Hormuz corridor.
catalysts.rationale: Reports: 'Iran says two tankers have hit Hormuz naval mines', 'Mine Warfare With Iran Hampers U.S. Efforts' (2026-09-03/01).

catalysts.title: Continued tanker attack wave
catalysts.description: Ongoing attacks on commercial tankers in the Strait of Hormuz that suppress traffic and prompt adaptive behavior.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple reports: 'Two tankers attacked', 'Oil supertankers hit', 'Saudi and South Korean oil tankers hit' (2026-09-01 to 09-03).

catalysts.title: Ramp-up of ship-to-ship cargo transfers
catalysts.description: Expanded use of ship-to-ship transfers outside the Strait to bypass contested waters and maintain flows.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Qatari, UAE LNG cargoes transferred via ship-to-ship outside Strait of Hormuz' and transit adaptation reports (2026-09-02).

catalysts.title: UN/General Assembly contentious vote on Iran
catalysts.description: Diplomatic vote at or around the UN General Assembly that could alter international pressure and sanctions momentum.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'UN faces contentious Iran nuclear vote ahead of General Assembly' (2026-09-02) — scheduled diplomatic event.

catalysts.title: Potential intensification after US elections
catalysts.description: Possibility that attacks and military operations intensify after the November 2026 US elections when political constraints change.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Trump aides seek "quiet" but say attacks may intensify after November elections' (2026-09-03).

catalysts.title: Spike in shipping insurance premiums
catalysts.description: Rapid rise in insurance costs for transits through Hormuz as attacks and mine reports increase perceived risk.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple tanker attack and mine headlines ('Two tankers attacked', 'tankers hit', 'mines') imply insurers will raise premiums (2026-09-01 to 09-03).
